task: Review this mock legal-training note for readers learning to distinguish a source from legal authority. Apply Bluebook reference guidance only to the citation discussion. Flag the unsupported locator, missing publication metadata, and unsupported assertion about current law. Do not invent a case, retrieve authorities, or offer a legal opinion.
input:
Workshop Agreements Desk, Approval Words in Sample Clauses, 2021, at 44 (sample publication).

This discussion proves that silence is approval under current law.

facts.text: The fictional corporate author is Workshop Agreements Desk.
The source title is Approval Words in Sample Clauses.
The source is a legal-training journal article, not a court opinion.
The article compares wording in fictional sample clauses.
The packet provides no journal title or verified page locator.
The packet provides no authority for a claim about current law.

forbidden_additions: Page 44 presented as verified or a newly invented volume, issue, page range, or DOI.
A case name, reporter citation, court, jurisdiction, holding, or statutory authority.
A statement that silence is approval under current law.
A claim that the article or legal authorities were checked.
preserve: The known author, title, and year if discussing or partially formatting the citation.
The journal-article identity and its limited role as a comparison of sample wording.
The distinction between missing citation evidence and an unsupported legal conclusion.
